provenance.derivation: Composed in the manner of kasane no irome, for autumn: 3 of our own published entries read as layers from the outermost inward — 山燃 yama-moe (#903917), then 稲穂 ina-ho (#D5AC5E), then 濃土 koi-tsuchi (#642E20). NOT a historical combination: no layer is asserted to reproduce a documented Heian kasane, and no value was read from any kasane table. Chosen by hand, not generated. Adjacent layers are separated by ΔE00 40.8, 50.7 under @irodora/color-difference 0.1.0 — each above the ΔE00 5 at which the product calls two items the same (FR-44), because a layering whose edges cannot be told apart is not one. Weights fall inward (1, 0.8, 0.6, 0.5) because each inner layer shows less than the one over it.
provenance.editorialNotes: Autumn at its most coloured: the burning-hill red (山燃) outermost, the gold of the rice ear (稲穂) at its edge, and a deep earth (濃土) as the lining. Red over gold over earth is the brocade the name means; the gold is the accent because it is the brightest layer and it shows only where the red parts. The name is ours (錦秋, "Autumn Brocade"), coined as a seasonal image the way the historical names are; it is not presented as a traditional kasane name.
